title: Small loyalties

body.heading: Speak well of the absent
paragraphs: How you talk about a friend when they are not there is the truest measure of loyalty — and the one most likely to be reported back. Defending the absent, or simply declining to join a pile-on, is a deposit nobody sees you make and everybody somehow knows about.
The reverse is also true, which is why rooms go quiet in a particular way when certain people leave them.

body.heading: Remember the small print
paragraphs: The interview on Thursday, the father’s operation, the fear of flying before the holiday — remembering these, and asking after them, is loyalty in its everyday uniform. It says: your life is filed in me under “matters,” not “miscellaneous.”
Nobody’s memory is perfect. Notes, reminders, and calendar entries are not cheating; they are loyalty with a system.

body.heading: Show up for the unglamorous
paragraphs: Anyone can attend the celebration. Loyalty is the airport pickup at midnight, the help with the landlord letter, the second pair of hands for the flat-pack wardrobe. Unglamorous help is remembered at a resolution glamorous help never reaches.
You will not manage it every time. Loyalty is a direction, not a record — and friends can tell the difference between a lapse and a pattern.

takeaway: Speak well of the absent, remember the small print, and show up for the unglamorous things.
